chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said:

I asked him about the pregnant woman who sees blood just as she used to see during the days of her menstruation, regularly every month. So he said: She should refrain from the Salat just as she used to do during her menstruation. So, when she is clean, she should pray.
ai.seo_question: How does a pregnant woman determine when to stop praying if she bleeds regularly like her period?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of istihada (non-menstrual bleeding) for pregnant women, establishing that regular, predictable bleeding is treated as hayd (menstruation) rather than irregular bleeding. It highlights the practical implication that such women are exempt from daily prayers during these specific days, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between natural physiological cycles and pathological bleeding. This ruling ensures that the burden of worship is adjusted according to the woman's specific condition, maintaining spiritual purity without unnecessary hardship.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al A’ala, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), said,

‘I asked himasws about the pregnant woman seeing the blood just as she would see during the days of her menstruation (Haydh), regularly, during every month. So heasws said: ‘She should refrain from the Salaat just as she would do during her menstruation (Haydh). So when she is clean, she should pray Salaat’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “I once asked one of the two Imam, (abu Ja‘far or abu ‘Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, about the case of a pregnant woman who experiences blood discharge like the days of her Hayd (menses) every month as a straight habit. He (the Imam) said, ‘She must hold herself back from Salah (prayer) like in days of her Hayd (menses), and when she is clean then perform Salah (prayer).”’
